subject: general
question: The average age of a father and his daughter is 27 years. The ratio of their ages 4 years hence from now, will be 23 : 8. Find the daughter's present age (in years).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present sum of ages = 27 × 2 = 54 years.

Sum of ages after 4 years = 54 + 8 = 62 years.

Total ratio parts after 4 years = 23 + 8 = 31 parts.

31 parts = 62 years ⇒ 1 part = 2 years.

Daughter's present age = (8 parts × 2) − 4 = 12 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average present age of father and daughter = 27 years

Ratio of their ages 4 years hence = 23 : 8

 Ages 4 Years Hence Total Sum = 54 (Present) + 8 = 62 years Father (23 units) 8 units 
 Total 31 units = 62 years → 1 unit = 2 years Daughter's Present Age = (8 × 2) − 4 = 12 years 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of their present ages = 27 × 2 = 54 years

⇒ Let the present age of the father be F and the daughter be D.

⇒ F + D = 54

⇒ After 4 years, Father's age = F + 4 and Daughter's age = D + 4

⇒ (F + 4) / (D + 4) = 23 / 8

⇒ 8 × (F + 4) = 23 × (D + 4)

⇒ 8F + 32 = 23D + 92

⇒ 8F − 23D = 60

⇒ Substituting F = 54 − D into the equation:

⇒ 8 × (54 − D) − 23D = 60

⇒ 432 − 8D − 23D = 60

⇒ 31D = 432 − 60

⇒ 31D = 372

⇒ D = 372 ÷ 31 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Ages Over Time

If the sum of ages of n people is S, then their sum of ages after t years will be S + nt, because each person's age increases by t years independently.

Change in Average Age

If the present average age of a group is A, their average age after t years will exactly be A + t. The new total sum will naturally be n × (A + t).

Age Ratio Interpretation

When setting up linear equations from word problems, "t years hence" always requires adding t to the present age variables, while "t years ago" requires subtracting t from the present age variables before applying any ratio comparison.
